title: Android Naming Conventions
description: Beginner-to-advanced naming reference for Kotlin declarations, Android layers and components, Gradle modules and variants, resources, Compose APIs, state, events, streams, tests, and implementation strategies.

sections.title: Core Kotlin Names
sections.description: Names should reveal the domain role without requiring type or implementation archaeology.

subtopics.title: Case & Declaration Quick Reference
subtopics.description: Follow Kotlin conventions unless an Android tool imposes a resource or manifest format.

table.title: Kotlin and Android Case Reference
rows: Use verbs for actions and predicates for booleans
Reserve for const val and true constants
Avoid underscores and redundant layer nesting
Composable functions that emit UI are noun-like
Encode feature, element, and role consistently

codeBlocks.code:
Package: com.example.payments.checkout (lowercase, no underscores)
Class/interface/object/typealias: PaymentRepository, CheckoutState (PascalCase)
Function/property/local/parameter: calculateTotal, selectedItem (camelCase)
Compile-time-style constant: MAX_RETRY_COUNT (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE)
Generic type: T, R, Key, Value, RequestT (concise or descriptive)
Resource/file identifier: checkout_submit_button (lower_snake_case)

callouts.title: Tooling Consistency Wins
callouts.text: Use the project's formatter and static analysis rules. Local consistency improves search and review even where more than one style is technically valid.

subtopics.title: Functions, Properties & Booleans
subtopics.description: Functions usually use verb phrases; properties use noun phrases; booleans read as assertions or capabilities.

tabs.label: Prefer
tabs.code:
fun calculateTotal(): Money
fun saveDraft(draft: Draft)
val selectedAccount: Account
val isLoading: Boolean
val hasUnsavedChanges: Boolean
val canSubmit: Boolean
val shouldShowRationale: Boolean

tabs.label: Avoid
tabs.code:
fun total(): Money       // action or property?
fun process(data: Data)   // says nothing about outcome
val loadingFlag: Boolean  // type-encoded suffix
val check: Boolean        // check what?
val data: Any             // domain meaning lost

callouts.title: Name the Outcome
callouts.text: Replace vague verbs such as handle, process, manage, do, and execute with the domain result: validateAddress, chargePayment, cacheProfile, or publishReceipt.

subtopics.title: Acronyms, Units & Encoded Context
subtopics.description: Treat acronyms as words in Pascal/camel case and include units when the type cannot express them.

codeBlocks.code:
class XmlParser
class HttpClient
val userId: UserId
val apiUrl: Url
val timeoutMillis: Long
val retryDelay: Duration
val distanceMeters: Double

callouts.title: Prefer Types Over Suffixes
callouts.text: Duration, Money, UserId, and other domain types prevent unit/identity confusion better than names alone. Keep a unit suffix at platform boundaries that still use primitives.

sections.title: Files, Packages & Modules
sections.description: Make navigation predictable from a symbol or feature name.

subtopics.title: Kotlin File Names
subtopics.description: Name a file after its primary declaration; use a descriptive PascalCase topic for related top-level declarations and extensions.

codeBlocks.code:
UserRepository.kt → UserRepository
CheckoutViewModel.kt → CheckoutViewModel
MoneyFormatting.kt → related money formatting functions
ContextExtensions.kt → only if extensions form one coherent Context topic
Avoid Utils.kt, Helpers.kt, Common.kt, Misc.kt

callouts.title: Utility Buckets Hide Cohesion
callouts.text: A growing Utils file usually contains several domain concepts. Split by responsibility so names communicate ownership and dependencies.

subtopics.title: Feature & Layer Packages
subtopics.description: Choose a consistent feature-first or layer-first structure. In larger apps, feature-first naming keeps related UI, domain, and data code discoverable.

codeBlocks.code:
com.example.app.feature.checkout.ui
com.example.app.feature.checkout.data
com.example.app.feature.checkout.domain
com.example.app.core.network
com.example.app.core.database

Gradle modules:
:feature:checkout
:core:network
:core:designsystem

callouts.title: Avoid Redundant Prefixes
callouts.text: Inside feature.checkout, names such as CheckoutCheckoutScreen or CheckoutFeatureRepository repeat context. Retain the domain word only when it distinguishes the public symbol during imports/search.

subtopics.title: Build Variants, Convention Plugins & Catalog Aliases
subtopics.description: Build names become command-line and CI APIs. Keep variants, modules, convention plugins, and version-catalog aliases predictable and free of redundant context.

codeBlocks.code:
Build types: debug, release, benchmark
Flavors: demo, production (one consistent flavor dimension)
Modules: :app, :feature:checkout, :core:network, :benchmark
Convention plugins: company.android.application, company.android.library.compose
Catalog aliases: androidx-lifecycle-runtime-compose, kotlinx-coroutines-test
Bundles: androidx-compose-ui, test-unit

callouts.title: Names Are Automation Contracts
callouts.text: Renaming a variant or module can break CI tasks, publishing, Baseline Profile wiring, and external consumers. Prefer durable domain/capability names and migrate automation deliberately.

sections.title: Android Components & Architecture Layers
sections.description: Use suffixes when they identify a real framework contract or architectural responsibility.

subtopics.title: Activity, Fragment, Service, Receiver & Worker
subtopics.description: Framework entry points keep conventional suffixes because the lifecycle contract matters.

callouts.title: Name the Responsibility, Not Screen Shape
callouts.text: Prefer CheckoutActivity or PlaybackService over generic BaseActivity2 or MyService. Abstract base types should state the behavior they standardize, if one is needed at all.

subtopics.title: Repositories, Data Sources & Use Cases
subtopics.description: Interfaces use the domain capability. Implementations name their strategy; data sources name the system boundary; use cases name a user/business action.

tabs.label: Contracts
tabs.code:
interface UserRepository
interface PaymentGateway
fun interface ValidateAddress
class SubmitOrder

tabs.label: Implementations
tabs.code:
class OfflineFirstUserRepository
class InMemoryUserRepository
class DefaultUserRepository // only when no meaningful strategy name exists
class HttpUserDataSource
class RoomUserDataSource
class FakeUserRepository

callouts.title: Avoid Impl When Strategy Exists
callouts.text: UserRepositoryImpl reveals no behavior. OfflineFirst, Cached, InMemory, Room, or Default helps readers choose and configure the implementation.

subtopics.title: Models Across Boundaries
subtopics.description: Use a simple domain name in its owning layer and a suffix only where several representations coexist or imports would be ambiguous.

codeBlocks.code:
data class UserDto(...)      // transport contract
@Entity data class UserEntity(...) // database schema
data class User(...)               // domain model
data class UserUiModel(...)        // presentation-only projection
data class UserPayload(...)        // outbound request when clearer than Dto

callouts.title: Suffixes Must Mean One Thing
callouts.text: Define DTO, Entity, Model, Payload, and UiModel meanings for the project. Do not use Model as a universal suffix on every class.

sections.title: State, Events, Streams & Async APIs
sections.description: Names should distinguish durable state, user actions, domain results, and changing streams.

subtopics.title: UiState & User Actions
subtopics.description: Name screen state after the screen; name action methods after the domain result rather than UI control details.

codeBlocks.code:
data class CheckoutUiState(
    val cartItems: List<CartItemUiModel>,
    val isSubmitting: Boolean,
    val validationErrors: Map<Field, String>
)

fun updateShippingAddress(address: Address)
fun submitOrder()
fun retryPayment()

// Avoid: onBlueButtonClicked(), handleEvent(), process()

callouts.title: Keep ViewModel Names UI-Agnostic
callouts.text: A ViewModel method may be called from touch, keyboard, voice, or another form factor. Name the business intent instead of the current widget.

subtopics.title: Private Mutable Backing Properties
subtopics.description: A leading underscore clearly pairs private mutable state with its immutable public view.

callouts.title: Use the Pattern Only for a Pair
callouts.text: Do not prefix every private property with an underscore. It is useful when both mutable backing and public property share the same conceptual name.

subtopics.title: Flow & Stream Names
subtopics.description: Properties use noun/state names. Functions that create or query changing data use an observe/get...Stream convention consistently; avoid unnecessary Flow suffixes when the type is obvious.

tabs.label: State Properties
tabs.code:
val uiState: StateFlow<ProfileUiState>
val connectivity: Flow<Connectivity>
val messages: Flow<List<Message>>

tabs.label: Repository Functions
tabs.code:
fun observeUser(id: UserId): Flow<User>
fun getUsersStream(): Flow<List<User>>
suspend fun getUser(id: UserId): User
suspend fun refreshUsers(): Result<Unit>

callouts.title: One-Shot vs Stream Must Be Obvious
callouts.text: A suspend getUser and Flow getUser with similar names invite misuse. Establish verbs such as observe or Stream for changing values and reserve refresh/sync/save for actions.

sections.title: Jetpack Compose Names
sections.description: Compose naming communicates whether an API emits UI, creates state, or extends Modifier.

subtopics.title: Composable Functions & Layers
subtopics.description: Composable functions that emit UI and return Unit use PascalCase nouns. Use Route for screen wiring and Screen/content names for stateless presentation when that project convention adds clarity.

callouts.title: Name What It Is
callouts.text: Prefer ProfileHeader and PaymentMethodPicker over RenderHeader or CreatePaymentView. Declarative UI functions describe an element, not an imperative rendering command.

subtopics.title: modifier, State & Callbacks
subtopics.description: Place modifier after required parameters and before optional parameters; callbacks use on + event/result names.

codeBlocks.code:
@Composable
fun AddressForm(
    address: AddressInput,
    onAddressChange: (AddressInput) -> Unit,
    onSubmit: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true
)

callouts.title: Callback Name Describes Occurrence
callouts.text: onClick is fine for a generic Button; a domain component should expose onSubmit, onAccountSelected, or onRetry so callers understand intent.

subtopics.title: Modifier Factories, CompositionLocals & Previews
subtopics.description: Modifier factories use camelCase extension names; CompositionLocals use a Local prefix; private previews use descriptive PascalCase names ending in Preview.

callouts.title: Avoid Modifier Suffix on Factories
callouts.text: Call sites already read Modifier.selectionOutline(...). Names like selectionOutlineModifier add redundant type information.

sections.title: Android Resource & Manifest Names
sections.description: Resource names are global within their type and should remain searchable, stable, and feature-oriented.

subtopics.title: Strings, IDs, Layouts & Drawables
subtopics.description: Use lower_snake_case with feature/component/purpose order; avoid screen position, temporary appearance, and translated words in identifiers.

codeBlocks.code:
string: checkout_submit_order, checkout_error_payment_declined
plurals: cart_item_count
id: checkout_email_field, checkout_submit_button
layout: activity_main, fragment_legacy_profile, item_order
drawable: ic_add_24, bg_checkout_card, illustration_empty_cart
menu: menu_order_details
navigation: nav_checkout
color: checkout_status_error (or design-system semantic token)

callouts.title: Name by Meaning, Not Current Appearance
callouts.text: red_text or left_button becomes wrong after redesign or RTL. Prefer error_text and previous_button; semantic names survive visual change.

subtopics.title: Formatted Strings & Plurals
subtopics.description: Name the complete message purpose. Add translator comments when placeholders or context are ambiguous.

codeBlocks.code:
<!-- Greeting shown on profile header; %1$s is display name. -->
<string name="profile_greeting">Hello, %1$s</string>
<plurals name="download_file_count">
    <item quantity="one">%d file</item>
    <item quantity="other">%d files</item>
</plurals>

callouts.title: Identifier Is Not Source Text
callouts.text: Resource keys should remain stable when wording changes. Use the message's role, not an English sentence transliterated into an identifier.

sections.title: Tests, Exceptions & Naming Review
sections.description: Tests should state behavior; exceptions should state failure; review names at API boundaries.

subtopics.title: Test Classes, Methods & Fixtures
subtopics.description: Test classes name the subject. Backtick test functions can read as behavior sentences; fixtures use domain roles rather than unexplained numbers.

callouts.title: Name Condition and Outcome
callouts.text: A test report should explain the broken rule without opening code. Include the relevant precondition and observable result, not implementation steps.

subtopics.title: Errors, Results & Exceptions
subtopics.description: Name exceptions as failures and result alternatives as domain outcomes; avoid catch-all Error when callers need recovery decisions.

callouts.title: Do Not Encode Transport in Domain Names
callouts.text: A domain layer usually cares about Unauthenticated or PaymentDeclined, not Http401Exception. Translate infrastructure details at the boundary.

subtopics.title: Naming Review Checklist
subtopics.description: A strong name is precise, searchable, consistent, durable, pronounceable, and appropriate to its abstraction level.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Name states domain meaning, not only type
□ Verb/noun/boolean grammar reads naturally
□ Acronyms and casing follow one convention
□ Units or domain value types prevent ambiguity
□ Implementation names reveal strategy, not Impl
□ Stream versus one-shot semantics are obvious
□ Mutable backing state is private and intentionally paired
□ Compose UI names are nouns; callbacks state events
□ Resource keys use feature + purpose and semantic wording
□ Test names state condition and result
□ Vague words (data, info, manager, helper, utils, process) are justified
□ Name will remain correct after likely UI/implementation changes

callouts.title: Rename During Design
callouts.text: If a precise name is difficult, the responsibility may be mixed or the abstraction unclear. Use naming friction to discover a better boundary before adding comments.
